About.title: About
About.p1: Nine-plus years building enterprise systems, integrations, and platforms, centered on Java (Spring Boot and Quarkus) with experience across frontend, mobile, and operations. I have worked as a software architect in consulting, led teams in fintech, and currently combine senior development with university teaching and entrepreneurship (Kahani E.A.S.).
About.p2: I focus on maintainable solutions tied to the business: clear module boundaries, explicit API contracts, observability, and repeatable deployments. I enjoy turning ambiguous requirements into designs teams can ship with confidence.
About.p3: My differentiator is end-to-end technical ownership: business → requirements → architecture → backend → frontend → infrastructure → CI/CD → production. I can take a project from the context diagram all the way to running it in production.

Ai.title: AI-Augmented Software Engineering
Ai.subtitle: How I use AI as part of the engineering workflow, with technical judgment and human review.
Ai.p1: I work with Claude, Codex, and OpenCode as part of the development cycle, backed by Spec-Driven Development: specs and architecture come first, and agents implement against them.
Ai.p2: AI accelerates, it does not decide: every change goes through tests and human review before reaching CI/CD, and project context lives in versioned documents inside the repository.
highlights: Spec-Driven Development: versioned specs and contracts before code.
AI-assisted code generation and architecture review with specialized agents.
Assisted testing and documentation, always with human-in-the-loop validation.
Project memory and context kept in the repository to stay coherent across sessions.

Decisions.title: How I make technical decisions
Decisions.subtitle: The criteria I apply when choosing architecture and platform.

items.title: Microservices vs. modular monolith
items.body: I start with clear domain boundaries and split services when there are operational, scalability, or ownership reasons.

items.title: Kubernetes vs. Docker Compose
items.body: Kubernetes when there is a real need for orchestration, high availability, or multiple workloads; Compose for small deployments where operational simplicity matters more.

items.title: Build vs. buy
items.body: I weigh operational cost, complexity, and dependency before adopting new infrastructure.
